newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B INDEX DOWN 1.5 PCT AT NOON ON LUJIAZUI.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B INDEX DOWN 1.5 PCT AT NOON ON LUJIAZUI.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares slumped around 1.5 percent in Tuesday morning trading, buffeted by further selling of Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co, brokers said.
The sell-off in Lujiazui started on Monday after the property developer announced lower-than-expected interim results for the first half of 1997, they said.
The B index ended Tuesday morning down 1.052 points or 1.45 percent to 71.658 points on light turnover of $2.418 million, compared with $3.396 million on Monday morning.

Lujiazui fell $0.118 or 9.93 percent -- close to its daily limit down of 10 percent -- to $1.070 on volume of around 1.02 million shares, making it the morning's biggest loser and most actively traded B share.
"Lujiazui's poor performance continued to push the market down because it has a heavy weighting in the index," said one analyst at a major domestic securities firm.
Lujiazui on Friday posted net profits of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, down 67 percent from the year-ago period.
Lujiazui still has more room to fall and its performance could drag the B share index down further, brokers said.
"I'm sure Lujiazui could go down more and I wouldn't be too surprised if it went below $1," said an analyst at a European securities firm in Shanghai.

Other developers with ties to Shanghai's Pudong development zone -- Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co and Shanghai Wai Gaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co -- may also face selling pressure, they said.
Of 47 B shares, 34 shares traded with 16 down, 13 up and five unchanged.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares also slid on Lujiazui, brokers said. The company lists both A and B shares in Shanghai.
The A index slipped 4.675 points or 0.38 percent to 1,234.891 points on turnover of 1.471 billion yuan against 2.225 billion on Monday morning.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 43.535 points or 1.17 percent to 3,692.294 points.
Brokers said both the A and B share markets could fall further on Tuesday afternoon due to Lujiazui.
Investors would focus on interim results in the short term since companies must report by the end of August, they said.
